"When one offers the *bali* to the beings, that sacrifice to the beings (*bhūtayajña*) is completed. "When one gives food to the Brahmins, that sacrifice to men (*manuṣyayajña*) is completed. "When one studies one's own Vedic recitation—even a single *ṛc*, *yajus*, or *sāman*—that sacrifice to Brahman (*brahmayajña*) is completed."

"If he studies the Ṛg-veda, streams of milk flow for him and carry the svadhā offering to his ancestors; if the Yajus-formulas, streams of clarified butter; if the Sāmans, Soma flows clear for them; if the Atharvans and Aṅgirases, streams of honey; if the Brāhmaṇas, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, Kalpas, Gāthās, and Nārāśaṃsīs, streams of fat flow and carry the svadhā offering to his ancestors."

When he studies the Ṛg-veda, he satisfies the gods with oblations of milk; when the Yajus-verses, with oblations of ghee; when the Sāmans, with oblations of Soma; when the Atharvāṅgirases, with oblations of honey; and when the Brāhmaṇas, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, Kalpas, Gāthās, and Nārāśaṃsīs, he satisfies the gods with oblations of fat. Being satisfied, they satisfy him in turn with long life, luster, splendor, prosperity, fame, Vedic glory, and the enjoyment of food. Thus it is said.
Thus ends the tenth Anuvāka in the second Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 10 ||

"One who is about to perform the *brahmayajña* should go out from the village toward the east, where no roof is visible, or toward the north, or toward the northeast; when the sun has risen, having arranged the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder, having sat down, having washed both hands, he should sip water three times, wipe his mouth twice, touch water once, and then touch his head, eyes, nostrils, ears, and heart."

In that he sips water three times, by that he gratifies the *ṛc*s; in that he wipes his mouth twice, by that the *yajus* formulas; in that he touches [the lips] once, by that the *sāman*s; in that he sprinkles his left hand and his feet, and touches his head, eyes, nostrils, ears, and heart, by that he gratifies the *Atharvāṅgiras*s, the *Brāhmaṇa*s, the *Itihāsas*, the *Purāṇas*, the *Kalpas*, the *Gāthās*, and the *Nārāśaṃsīs*.

"Having spread out a large quantity of darbha grass and made a seat for his lap, he should sit facing the east and study his sacred recitation (svādhyāya). For darbha grass is the essence of waters and plants; thus he makes the Brahman possessed of essence. Having placed his hands and feet with the right over the left and holding the purifiers (pavitra), he begins with "Oṃ," for this sacrificial formula (yajus) is the voice that corresponds to the threefold knowledge (trayī vidyā); it is the supreme syllable. This very thing has been declared by a Ṛg verse: [The verse follows: "The seers who, through their insight, beheld the hidden light within the highest heaven... etc.

"In the imperishable syllable of the Ṛgveda, in the highest heaven, upon which all the gods are seated—he who does not know that, what will he do with the Ṛgveda? But those who know it, they have attained their seat. Thus [it is said]. He employed only three [words]: "bhūr bhuvaḥ svar"—he employed that which is indeed the truth of speech; whatever is the truth of speech, that he employed. Then he recites the Sāvitrī Gāyatrī three times: foot by foot, half-verse by half-verse, and without pausing. Savitṛ is the progenitor of prosperity; verily he obtains prosperity. Moreover, by means of this well-known opening, he enters upon the meters.
Thus ends the eleventh anuvāka of the second prapāṭhaka in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 11 ||

"In a village, one should study the *svādhyāya* with the mind, by day or by night"—thus indeed said Śauceya Āhneya. "Furthermore, whether in the forest, when weak, or by means of speech; whether standing, walking, sitting, or lying down—one should certainly study the *svādhyāya*. The ascetic who, knowing this, studies the *svādhyāya*, becomes meritorious. "Salutation to Brahman! Salutation be to Agni! Salutation to the Earth! Salutation to the Plants!"

"Salutation to Speech; salutation to the Lord of Speech; salutation to the great Viṣṇu, I offer. Thus ends the twelfth anuvāka in the second prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"At midday one should study with great intensity; for this Brāhmaṇa is indeed that very Sun, and therefore it burns most fiercely at that time. Regarding this, there is this verse: 'The brilliant array of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. It has filled the heaven, the earth, and the intermediate space. Sūrya is the soul of all that moves and stands.'"

"This very sacrifice is extended on the same day and is completed on the same day; its final purificatory bath (avabhṛtha) takes place before evening. "He recites the concluding verse, 'Homage to Brahman,' three times. "Having touched water, he goes to his home; then whatever he gives constitutes the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā)."
Thus ends the thirteenth anuvāka in the second prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 13 ||

"Of this very sacrifice, the cloud is the *havirdhāna* (the vessel for the oblation), lightning is the fire, rain is the oblation, thunder is the *vaṣaṭkāra*, and when it crashes, that is the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*. Vāyu is the self, and the new moon (*amāvāsyā*) is the *sviṣṭakṛt*. Thus, he who knows this studies his own sacred texts (*svādhyāya*) while it is raining from the cloud, while it is lightning, while it is thundering, while it is crashing, or while the purifying wind is blowing, on the day of the new moon; he indeed performs austerity, for the study of one's own sacred texts is austerity.

The most excellent one ascends to the highest heaven and becomes the most excellent among his equals. Indeed, as much as one wins the heavenly world by giving this earth filled with wealth, so much a world does he win; moreover, he wins a greater and inexhaustible [world], conquers repeated death, and attains union with Brahman. Thus ends the fourteenth anuvāka in the second prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"Of this very sacrifice there are two occasions when study is suspended: when one is impure oneself, and when the place is impure. "The deities are prosperity. He who, knowing this, studies his own portion of the Veda (*svādhyāya*)—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, in the forest or in the village—as much as he has strength for, conquers all worlds; debtless toward all worlds, he moves through them. Regarding this, it is said: "May we be debtless in this world, debtless in the next, and debtless in the third world."

"May we pass through all paths—the paths of the gods and the paths of the fathers—free from debt. When Agni was born, evil seized him; the gods drove away that evil with oblations, [evil] from the oblations by means of the sacrifice, from the sacrifice by means of the sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*), from the sacrificial fees by means of the Brahmin, from the Brahmin by means of the meters (*chandas*), and from the meters by means of private Vedic study (*svādhyāya*). Private Vedic study is the remover of evil; it is indeed the purifier of the gods. He who neglects it becomes one who has no share in speech, and no share in the heavenly vault (*nāka*). Regarding this, there is this verse: [The verse follows: "The path of the fathers and the path of the gods... etc.

"He who has abandoned a friend who knows [him as] a friend—of him there is no share even in what is spoken. Even if he hears it, he hears it without ears; for he does not know the path of righteous action. Therefore, one's own Veda must be studied. Whatever sacrifice one studies, by that very act his desired goal is accomplished; he attains union (*sāyujya*) with Agni, Vāyu, and Āditya. Regarding this, the following verse is recited:

"Whether they speak of one who is recent or of one who is ancient, whoever speaks around a man who knows the Veda—they are all speaking around Āditya alone; Agni is the second, and Haṃsa is the third. "As many deities as there are, they all dwell in a Brāhmaṇa who knows the Veda. Therefore, one should pay homage day after day to those Brāhmaṇas who know the Veda, and one should not utter anything vulgar toward them; thus one gratifies these very deities."
Thus ends the fifteenth anuvāka in the second prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 15 ||

"Indeed, he is emptied here; he is truly emptied who officiates at a sacrifice or accepts a gift. Having officiated at a sacrifice or having accepted a gift, he should recite the Veda as his private study (*svādhyāya*) three times without eating. Or, for three nights, he should extend the *Sāvitrī* Gāyatrī [by repetition]. A choice boon (*vara*) is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*); by means of a boon, he protects the boon, for the self is indeed the boon. Thus ends the sixteenth section (*anuvāka*) in the second chapter (*prapāṭhaka*) of the *Kṛṣṇayajurvedīya Taittirīyāraṇyaka*.

"Verily, he who officiates at a sacrifice milks the meters. Therefore, by whatever sacrificial rite one should officiate, that person, having gone to the forest and sitting in a pure place, should remain reciting his own sacred study (*svādhyāya*). For him, fasting is the initiation (*dīkṣā*); standing [in meditation] is the *upasad* ceremony; sitting is the pressing day (*sutyā*); speech is the *juhū* ladle; mind is the *upabhṛt* ladle; the offering is the *dhruvā* ladle; breath is the oblation; the *Sāman* is the *adhvaryu* priest. Indeed, this sacrifice has breath as its sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), it has an infinite sacrificial fee, and it is most prosperous."
Thus ends the seventeenth section in the second chapter of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"In how many ways does the *avakīrṇin* enter? The exponents of Brahman say: 'In four ways—he enters Maruts with his vital breaths, Indra with his strength, Bṛhaspati with his sacred luster (*brahmavarcasa*), and Agni with all that remains. Sudeva Kāśyapa discovered this expiation for him."

If a student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārin*) should spill his semen on the night of the new moon, he should carry forward the fire, kindle it, and offer two oblations of clarified butter, dipping it twice, with the mantras: "I have spilled [semen] out of desire; I have spilled it, O Desire! To Desire, Svāhā! I have been milked out by desire; I have been milked out, O Desire! To Desire, Svāhā! For clarified butter is indeed immortality; thus he places immortality within himself. Having offered the oblation, with hands joined in reverence, he should address the fire from a slightly oblique direction: "May the Maruts sprinkle me; may Indra sprinkle me; may Bṛhaspati sprinkle me."

"May this Agni sprinkle me with long life and with strength; make me possessed of long life," he says. Thus the Maruts bestow breaths upon him, Indra bestows strength, Bṛhaspati bestows spiritual luster, and the other Agni bestows everything else. Having become whole in every limb, he attains a full span of life.

"One should consecrate [the water] three times, for the gods are true to the three. He who might feel himself as if unpurified should sacrifice in this manner and consecrate in this manner; thus he purifies himself and bestows life-span upon himself. The sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) is a choice gift; by means of a choice gift, one wins what is choice, for the self is indeed the choice gift.
Thus ends the eighteenth anuvāka in the second prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"I take refuge in Bhūḥ; I take refuge in Bhuvaḥ; I take refuge in Svaḥ; I take refuge in Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ. I take refuge in Brahman; I take refuge in the treasury of Brahman; I take refuge in the Immortal; I take refuge in the treasury of the Immortal. I take refuge in that four-netted treasury of Brahman which Death does not perceive. I take refuge in the Gods; I take refuge in the city of the Gods. Enveloped, well-enveloped by the armor and splendor of Kaśyapa, [I am protected] by Brahman."

"That to which [the word] *namas* belongs is its head; *dharma* is the crown of the head; *brahman* is the upper jaw; *yajña* is the lower jaw; *viṣṇu* is the heart; *saṃvatsara* is the organ of generation; the two *aśvins* are the two front feet; *atri* is the middle; *mitra* and *varuṇa* are the two hind feet; *agni* is the first section of the tail; after that, *indra*; after that, *prajāpati*; and *abhaya* (fearlessness) is the fourth. This, indeed, is the celestial *śākvara* porpoise; "him, indeed," [so it is said].

"Whoever knows this conquers repeated death, conquers the heavenly world; he does not die on a journey, he does not die in fire, he does not die in water, he does not die childless, and he becomes one who eats light food. "You are the firm; you are the abode of the firm; you are the lord of beings; you are the best of beings; toward you all beings turn around. Homage to you! Homage to all! Homage to us! Homage to the infant, homage to the youth! Thus.
Thus ends the nineteenth anuvāka of the second prapāṭhaka in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"Salutation to the eastern quarter and to those deities who dwell therein; salutation to them. Salutation to the southern quarter and to those deities who dwell therein; salutation to them. Salutation to the western quarter and to those deities who dwell therein; salutation to them. Salutation to the northern quarter and to those deities who dwell therein; salutation to them. Salutation to the upward quarter and to those deities who dwell therein; salutation to them."

"Salutations, salutations to the downward direction and to the deities who dwell therein; salutations to the intermediate direction and to the deities who dwell therein. Salutations to those who dwell between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā; may they, with gracious souls, increase my long life. Salutations to the sages between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā; salutations, salutations to the sages between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā. Thus.
Thus ends the twentieth Anuvāka in the second Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 20 ||

With the *rakṣas* [verse], when the gods played with the seventeen; with the fifteen, for your life-span; the thirty-four for Vaiśvānara; the twenty-six, the Vātaraśanas, with the *kūṣmāṇḍa* verses; the five, with the *brahmayajña*; in the village, at midday; his indeed is the cloud; his indeed are two; it is emptied; he milks; how manyfold is the *avakīrṇin*? "Earth! Homage!"—the eastern one, twenty; together with the Vātaraśanas; he milks; the twenty-four.
Homage to Brahman; homage be to Agni; homage to the Earth; homage to the plants. Homage to Speech; homage to the Lord of Speech; homage to the great Viṣṇu do I render.
Oṃ. Peace, peace, peace.
Thus ends the second chapter of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 2 ||

Now begins the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Hariḥ Oṃ. We choose that auspiciousness which is health for the sacrifice and health for the lord of the sacrifice. May there be divine well-being for us; may there be well-being for human beings. May the healing medicine rise upward; may it be well with our bipeds and well with our quadrupeds.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!

"Oṃ! Consciousness is the offering-spoon; thought is the clarified butter; speech is the altar; what has been meditated upon is the sacrificial grass; insight is the fire; discernment is the fire; the Lord of Speech is the Hotṛ priest; the mind is the Upavaktṛ priest; breath is the oblation; the Sāman is the Adhvaryu priest. "O Lord of Speech, O Ordainer by name! May we worship your name. Do you ordain our name. Let the Lord of Speech drink the Soma. May he bestow manly vigor upon us—Svāhā! Thus [ends] the fifth [section] of the Adhvaryu.
Thus ends the first section (anuvāka) of the third chapter (prapāṭhaka) of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 1 ||

"Earth is the Hotṛ; Heaven is the Adhvaryu; Rudra is the Agnīdh; Bṛhaspati is the Upavaktṛ. "O Lord of Speech, with the power of speech, most perfectly gathered, you shall sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificer; bring him what is desirable; bestow excellent wealth upon him. The Lord of Speech drinks the Soma; he has generated Indra for the sake of sensory power—Svāhā! Thus [ends the section]; "Earth is the Hotṛ" is the tenth [verse].
Thus ends the second anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"Agni is the Hotṛ; the Aśvins are the Adhvaryus; Tvaṣṭṛ is the Agnīdh; Mitra is the Upavaktṛ. "Soma is the precursor of Soma; Śukra is the precursor of Śukra. These Somas of yours have been drunk, O Indra, by Vātāpi, who hears the invocation—Svāhā! Thus ends the section "Agni is the Hotṛ," consisting of eight [verses].
Thus ends the third Anuvāka in the third Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 3 ||

"May the sun be your eye; the wind your breath; the sky your back; the intermediate space your self; the sacrifice your limbs; the earth your body. "O Lord of Speech, with unimpaired speech, with an unimpaired ladle, impel the Hotṛ-offering that increases the gods in heaven—Svāhā! Thus ends the ninth [section] concerning the sun.
Thus ends the fourth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

Mahāhavis is the Hotṛ; Satyahavis is the Adhvaryu; Acyutapāja is the Agnīdh; Acyutamanas is the Upavaktṛ; Anādhṛṣya and Apratidhṛṣya are the two Abhigars of the sacrifice; Ayāsya is the Udgātṛ. O Vācaspati, O you who know the heart, our name! We honor your name; do you honor our name. Vācaspati has drunk the Soma. May the divine thread not be severed, nor the human one. Homage to Heaven! Homage to Earth! Svāhā! And [the verses] beginning with "apātrīṇi."
Thus ends the fifth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 5 ||

"Speech is the Hotṛ; the consecration is the wife; the wind is the Adhvaryu; the waters are the Abhigara; the mind is the oblation; I offer it into austerity. "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Brahman is self-existent. To the self-existent Brahman, svāhā!
Thus ends the ninth section on Speech as the Hotṛ.
Thus ends the sixth section in the third chapter of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"Brāhmaṇa is the Ekahotṛ; he is the sacrifice. May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may the sacrifice also be mine. "Agni is the Dvihotṛ; he is the sustainer. May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may the sustainer also be mine. "The Earth is the Trihotṛ; she is the foundation. May she grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may the foundation also be mine. "The Atmosphere is the Caturhotṛ; it is the various stations."

"May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may stability also be mine. Vāyu is the Pañcahotṛ; he is the vital breath (*prāṇa*). "May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may the vital breath also be mine. Candramas is the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ; he ordains the seasons. "May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may the seasons also be ordained for me. Food is the Saptahotṛ; it is the breath of the vital breath.

"May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may my vital breath become even more vital. The Sky is the Eight-Hotṛ; he is invincible. "May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may I become invincible. The Sun is the Nine-Hotṛ; he is radiant. "May he grant me offspring, cattle, prosperity, and glory; may I become radiant. Prajāpati is the Ten-Hotṛ; he is all this.

May he grant me offspring, cattle, nourishment, and glory; may everything be mine. May I have stability and vital breath that is unassailable; may everything be mine. The Brāhmaṇa is the sacrifice, Agni is the sustainer, the earth is the foundation, the intermediate space is the support, Vāyu is the vital breath, and the Moon is the seasons. He is food; he is the breath of breath; the sky is the unassailable; Āditya is the radiant; Prajāpati is all this—may everything be mine.
Thus ends the seventh Anuvāka in the third Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 7 ||

Agni [is joined] with the *yajus* formulas; Savitṛ with the *stomas*; Indra with the *ukthas* and *amadas*; Mitra and Varuṇa with the *āśis* (benedictions); the Aṅgirases with the *dhiṣṇiya* fires; the Maruts with the *sadas* and *havirdhāna* sheds; the Waters with the sprinkling waters (*prokṣaṇīs*); the Plants with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); Aditi with the altar (*vedi*); Soma with the consecration (*dīkṣā*); Tvaṣṭṛ with the fuel-wood (*idhma*); Viṣṇu with the sacrifice (*yajña*); the Vasus with the clarified butter (*ājya*); the Ādityas with the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*); the Viśve Devas with strength (*ūrj*); Pūṣan with the cry of "Svaga"; and Bṛhaspati with the office of the domestic priest (*purodhā*).

"Prajāpati by means of the Udgītha; the intermediate space by means of the Pavitra; Vāyu by means of the vessels; and I by means of faith"—thus [he says]. And [he says], "by means of initiation and the vessels, and one."
Thus ends the eighth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 8 ||

Senā is the [speech] of Indra; Dhenā of Bṛhaspati; Pathyā of Pūṣan; Vāc of Vāyu; Dīkṣā of Soma; Pṛthivī of Agni; Gāyatrī of the Vasus; Triṣṭubh of the Rudras; Jagatī of the Ādityas; Anuṣṭubh of Viṣṇu; Virāj of Varuṇa; Paṅkti of the Sacrifice; Anumati of Prajāpati; Śraddhā of Mitra; Prasūti of Savitṛ; Marīci of Sūrya; Rohiṇī of Candramas; Arundhatī of the Ṛṣis; and Vidyut of Parjanya.

The four quarters; the four intermediate quarters; day and night; agriculture and rain; brilliance and honor; water and plants; nourishment and truth—the wives of the gods. Thus [ends] the Anuṣṭubh consisting of the quarters and six [syllables].
Thus ends the ninth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I receive you. May King Varuṇa lead you. O divine Dakṣiṇā, this gold is for Agni; through it may I attain immortality. May there be vigor for the giver; may there be joy for me, the receiver. Who has given this to whom? Desire has given to Desire. Desire is the giver; Desire is the receiver. Enter the ocean of Desire. With Desire I receive you. O Desire, this is yours.

"O Kāma, this is your sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). May Uttaṅga Āṅgirasa accept you. A garment for Soma; a cow for Rudra; a horse for Varuṇa; a human being for Prajāpati; a bed for Manu; a she-goat for Tvaṣṭṛ; a ram for Pūṣan; a mule and a donkey for Nirṛti; an elephant for Himavat; a garland and ornaments for the Gandharvas and Apsarases; grain for the Viśvedevas; food for Vāc; boiled rice for Brahman; and water for the Ocean.

"Upon the outstretched one, the descendant of Aṅgiras; for Vaiśvānara, the chariot. "Vaiśvānara has ascended to the firmament as of old, to the back of heaven, being praised with hymns. Like the ancients, he has generated wealth for living beings; watchful, he traverses the common path. "May King Varuṇa lead you, O goddess Dakṣiṇā, to the chariot for Vaiśvānara. Through him, may I attain immortality. May there be vigor for the giver; may there be joy for me, the receiver. Who has given this to whom?"

Desire is for the sake of desire; Desire is the giver; Desire is the receiver. Enter the ocean that is Desire. With Desire I receive you. O Desire, this is yours. This, O Desire, is your sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). May Utāna Āṅgirasa receive you. Thus [it is said]. The giver [is] a man; the waters [are] for the receiver; nine [verses].
Thus ends the tenth Anuvāka in the third Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

He has discovered the golden, glowing, longing one; the self of Indra moving tenfold within the ocean, wandering with his mind. The Brahman, the Daśahotṛ, found him in the flood. Having entered within, he is the ruler of people; being one, he moves in many ways. Where the hundred pure lights become one, where all the Vedas become one, where all the Hotṛ-priests become one—he is the mental self of people.

"The Teacher has entered within, the Self of all people; wherein all creatures become one. Wherein the four *hotṛ*-priests attain perfection with the gods—he is the mental Self of people. "Brahmā, Indra, Agni, the foundation of the world; the Self of heaven, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati; the four *hotṛ*-priests, fashioned according to the quarters—he discovered the power of speech through austerity. "This is the Creator who has entered within."

"Tvaṣṭṛ, who transforms forms, the wise one; this sacrifice, the breath of immortality—sages have discerned him as the self of the four *hotṛ*s. "Brahman, Indra, Agni, the foundation of the world; the self of heaven, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati; the four *hotṛ*s, fashioned according to the quarters—he discovered through austerity the power of speech. "This creator who has entered within, Tvaṣṭṛ, who transforms forms, the wise one."

"The wise have discerned this sacrifice as the life-breath of immortality, the very self of the four officiating priests (hotṛs). "The wise have discerned this King Indra, this Savitṛ, the very self of Vāyu; him who shines intensely in the midst of the rays, whom the wise guard at the station of Cosmic Order (ṛta). "He who, unbroken, sustains the world within the cosmic egg (āṇḍakośa) and yet beholds the worlds from within; whose cosmic egg they call vigor (śuṣma), and whose membrane is the life-breath (prāṇa)—by that immortal one I am fashioned."

"The golden vessel, enveloped in dust, the radiant abode of treasures for the gods—filled with nectar, they perceive it as a mere fraction; they have certainly not discovered even a quarter of the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ. "By whom the seasons were fashioned fivefold, or indeed sixfold by the mind—him, the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ, who is being fashioned along with the seasons, the seers establish at the station of Cosmic Order (Ṛta). "This agent who has entered within, moving within the moon by means of the mind..."

"The gods do not perceive him who exists together with them, though he moves as the self of Indra in a hundred ways. "Indra is the king who rules over the world; he is the seven-hotṛ, fashioned in seven ways. "Beyond the thread being sprinkled around, moving within the sun with his mind—the Brahman discovered the heart of the gods. "The Brahman brought forth this Brahman, the flowing light in the midst of the ocean. "In whom the seven rivers..."

"He bestows abundant prosperity; O Indra, [prosperity] consisting of many horses and cattle"—thus. "The unshakable, abundant prosperity; that golden-hued one, the best finder of wealth, the filler, swells for Indra"—thus. "O Indra, [prosperity] consisting of many horses and cattle; the unshakable, abundant prosperity—may Indra bestow it upon me"—thus. "A hundred times a hundred are his harnessed bay steeds; may Indra, the ray of light, come hither with the Vasus, not shrinking away from the abundant prosperity; may Indra, the ray of light, the impeller, bestow it upon me"—thus.

"May this Agni place within me clarified butter as splendor, honeyed sensory power. "Hari, the winged bird, the gliding one, the fair-winged; he who dwells in heaven and moves through the sky—may he, as Indra, grant us our heart's desire. "The broad five-spoked wheel revolves, a golden light in the midst of the ocean; the imperishable light moves, gliding through the sky—may he, as Indra, grant us our heart's desire. "Seven yoke the chariot with its single wheel."

"The single horse bears [the world], having seven names; it is a three-naved wheel, undecaying and unsurpassed, by which all these worlds stand. "Beholding the auspicious, the seers who have found the light of heaven (*svarvid*) approached in the beginning with austerity and consecration (*dīkṣā*). From that, sovereignty, strength, and vigor were born. May the gods bow down toward this for him. "They have perceived Indra in the highest heaven—the white ray, the one being enjoyed, the leader of the waters, the guardian of the world."

The ruddy ones, tawny, uniform; flowing, tawny, uniform; hundreds, thousands, millions of navigable rivers—this is the white ray which encompasses this entire world. May it grant us progeny, cattle, and wealth. The white ray has encompassed everything; may it produce for me cattle of every form. The winged one, anointed by the magic power (*māyā*) of the Asura—the wise behold him with the heart, with the mind.

"Within the ocean, the sages perceive; the wise seek the station of the rays. "The bird bears speech with his mind; the Gandharva spoke it within the womb. "That shining, celestial inspired thought, the sages guard at the station of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*). "Those domestic animals of all forms—though diverse in appearance, they are of one form in many ways—may the god Agni release them first, Prajāpati in harmony with his progeny."
"O braid, in every plait! Bestow it upon us both! Further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice! Thus [he says].

"May there be delight here for those seven domestic animals which are multiform—though diverse in appearance, they are of one form in many ways—for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for heroic vigor. "May Vāyu, the god, first release those wild animals which are multiform—though diverse in appearance, they are of one form in many ways—Prajāpati, in harmony with his offspring. "The gods discovered the moving and unmoving world, rich in ghee, that had been hidden in secret, as the portion of Iḍā."

"May those wild animals of all forms—though diverse in appearance, they are manifold yet of one form—find delight here among these seven; for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, and for great heroism. "The self of people, the wise one who transforms, the supporter of creatures, the sovereign Virāj who moves—the One-Wheeled One (Ekacakra) has bestowed upon me the world of cows through his creative power (māyā). O God, [there are] eight of one form."
Thus ends the eleventh anuvāka of the third prapāṭhaka in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 11 ||

"The Puruṣa has a thousand heads; he has a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. Having pervaded the earth on all sides, he stood beyond it by the measure of ten fingers. This Puruṣa alone is all this—that which has been and that which is to be. He is the Lord of immortality, as well as of that which grows by food. Such is his greatness, and yet the Puruṣa is even greater than this. All beings constitute one quarter of him; his three quarters are the immortal in heaven. The Puruṣa rose upward with three quarters; one quarter of him came into being here again.

"Then he strode out in all directions, toward both the eating and the non-eating. From that, the Virāj was born; from the Virāj, the Puruṣa. Once born, he extended beyond—behind the earth and also before it. "When the gods performed the sacrifice with the Puruṣa as the oblation, the spring was its clarified butter, the summer the fuel, and the autumn the offering. Seven were its enclosing sticks; thrice seven were the fuel-sticks prepared. Thus did the gods, while performing the sacrifice...

“They bound the Puruṣa as the sacrificial animal. They sprinkled that sacrifice upon the sacred grass—the Puruṣa who was born in the beginning. With him, the gods sacrificed, as did the Sādhyas and the Ṛṣis. From that sacrifice, from which everything was offered, the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) was gathered; he created those animals belonging to Vāyu, both those of the forest and those of the village. From that sacrifice, from which everything was offered, the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born; the meters were born from it, and from it the Yajus-formulas were produced.

From him were born horses, and whatever animals have two rows of teeth; from him cows were born, and from him goats and sheep were produced. When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they arrange him? What was his mouth, what were his arms, what were his thighs, and what are his feet called? The Brāhmaṇa became his mouth; the Rājanya was made his arms; that which was his thighs became the Vaiśya; from his feet the Śūdra was born. From his mind the moon was born; from his eye the sun was born.

"From his mouth Indra and Agni were born; from his breath Vāyu was born. "From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved; from his feet the earth, and from his ears the quarters. Thus they fashioned the worlds. "I know this great Puruṣa, resplendent as the sun, beyond the darkness. Having surveyed all forms and created their names, the Wise One remains calling them by those names. "The Creator (Dhātṛ) proclaimed him in the beginning."

Śakra, the wise one, knows the four quarters. He who knows him thus becomes immortal here; there is no other path for proceeding. By means of sacrifice, the gods sacrificed with the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances (dharmas). Those great ones attained the height of heaven, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. Puruṣa was born in the beginning, in front; they fashioned the two seats.
Thus ends the twelfth section in the third chapter of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"Born from the waters and from the essence of the earth, he arose from Viśvakarman. Tvaṣṭṛ, fashioning his form, enters him. That Puruṣa’s entire birth was in the beginning. "I know this great Puruṣa, resplendent like the sun, beyond darkness. Knowing him thus, one becomes immortal here; there is no other path for going. "Prajāpati moves within the womb; though unborn, he is born in many ways."

"The wise perceive his source; the sages seek the station of the rays. "He who shines upon the gods, he who is the domestic priest of the gods, he who was born before the gods—to the radiant one, the Brahmanic, be homage! "Generating the Brahmanic luster, the gods spoke thus in the beginning: 'Whosoever knows this as a Brāhmaṇa, the gods shall be under his control. "Modesty and Fortune are thy two wives; day and night are thy sides; the stars are thy form."

"The Aśvins [have opened] the wide mouth; may I desire what is sacrificed; may I desire that person; may I desire everything. Thus [it is said]. "He is born under control," and there are seven [verses].
Thus ends the thirteenth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

Being the sustainer, he is sustained; he himself sustains. One God has entered manifoldly. When he grows weary of bearing the burden, having laid down the burden, he goes again to his setting. They call him both Death and Immortality; they call him the Sustainer and the Protector. He, being sustained and being nourished, sustains. He who knows him as the one to be sustained by Truth—this one abandons the newborn, and yet he does not abandon the aged; this one alone has carried away many in a single day.

"The tireless god is ever to be implored. "He who knows from whence he came into being, and the bond which he established with the Brahman—he rejoices in that, even when grown old and lying down; it does not abandon him throughout the ancient days. "All the waters flow after you, knowing you, purifying themselves like a calf with milk. "You kindle Agni, the bearer of oblations; you, Mātariśvan, are the sustainer of all creatures. "You are the sacrifice, and you indeed are Soma."

"All the gods come to your call; you alone have entered into many. Homage be to you; be easy for me to invoke. "Homage be to you both; hear my call, O Prāṇa and Apāna who move swiftly together. I invoke you both with a sacred prayer (brahman) to this rescue: abandon him who hates me, O youthful ones. Thus, Prāṇa and Apāna, being in agreement, abandon him. "Do not unite with the life-breath of that man. O gods, being in agreement with my sacred prayer, [abandon him]."

"I shall slay him who was given for slaughter. He brought forth the non-existent from the existent; whatever he brought forth, he became its protector. When he grew weary of bearing the burden, that burden of his passed away back again. Thus, you indeed became the vital breath (*prāṇa*); a great enjoyment for Prajāpati, a limb yet to be employed, since you have caused the nine gods to breathe. You two shall go to one of the creatures, [leaving] the nine.
Thus ends the fourteenth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"The gods follow Hari as he departs, the Lord of all, the bull of prayers. May the Brahman, which is of like form, follow my thought. Do not obstruct my path; stride forth! O Death, do not cut me off, do not slay me; do not take away my strength."

"Unbind me, do not steal from me; do not harm my offspring, O fierce one, nor my life. We shall worship you, the beholder of men, with an oblation. "To Death who desires [us] this very day, who makes us tremble—may the quarters of space listen to him for our sake; through desire, they have brought him back again. "By desire has desire come to me, from heart to heart, from Death. That which is their beloved there, let that come unto me. "Go away, O Death, along your own path, which is other than the way of the gods."

"To you who have eyes and hear, I speak: do not harm our offspring, nor our heroes. Thus, praising with my mind the ancient one, beseeching the bull of the people—he who is the sole ruler over human progeny—I worship Death, the first-born of Immortality. [This section consists of verses addressed] to Death; [there are] four [additional verses].
Thus ends the fifteenth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 15 ||

O Sūrya, you are the one who carries us across, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm. You are taken with a support; I take you for the resplendent Sūrya. This is your womb; I take you for the resplendent Sūrya.
Thus ends the sixteenth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
"Swell up, O most exhilarating Soma, with all your protections; be for us most extensive."
Thus ends the seventeenth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 17 ||
"Those mortals who saw the earlier Uṣas as she was shining forth have passed away; she has now become visible to us. And those who shall see her in future days, they too shall pass away."
Thus ends the eighteenth anuvāka in the third prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

"I settle you, the luminous one; I settle you, the light-maker; I settle you, the knower of light; I settle you, the radiant one; I settle you, the blazing one; I settle you, the one becoming resonant with *malmala*; I settle you, the shining one; I settle you, the gleaming one; I settle you, the unceasing one; I settle you, the one of great light; I settle you, the awakener; I settle you, the ever-watchful one. Thus.
Thus ends the nineteenth anuvāka of the third prapāṭhaka in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 19 ||

To exertion, svāhā! To effort, svāhā! To fatigue, svāhā! To exhaustion, svāhā! To rising, svāhā! To despondency, svāhā! To purity, svāhā! To sorrow, svāhā! To the state of being heated, svāhā! To the one who heats, svāhā! To the murder of a Brahmin, svāhā! To everything, svāhā! Thus.
Thus ends the twentieth Anuvāka in the third Prapāṭhaka of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.

One offers the mind with the liver to Bhava, Rudra with the spleen, Paśupati with the thick heart, Agni with the heart, Rudra with the blood, Śarva with the kidneys, Mahādeva with the inner ribs, and Oṣiṣṭhahan to Śiṅgīnikośya with the two kidneys; thus, the mind is one.
Thus ends the twenty-first Anuvāka of the third Prapāṭhaka in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 21 ||

Citti; Pṛthivī; Agni; Sūrya is your eye; Mahāhavis; Hotṛ; Vāk is the Hotṛ; Brāhmaṇa is the Ekahotṛ; Agni with the Yajus formulas; the army of the god Indra; Suvarṇa; Gharma; Sahasraśīrṣā; the sustainer from the waters; Hari; Taraṇi; Āpyāyasva; Eyuṣṭe; Jyotiṣmatī; Prayāsāya; Citta; twenty-one. || 21 ||
Cittir Agni, Prajāpati, has entered within by means of the Yajus-formulas; may we be united with him through offspring—of him, the wise ones [speak] the luminous fifty-three-fold [hymn]. 53.

We choose that auspiciousness and well-being; a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of the sacrifice. May there be divine prosperity for us; may there be prosperity for human beings. May the healing medicine ascend upward; may it be well with our bipeds, may it be well with our quadrupeds.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.
Thus ends the third chapter of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. || 3 ||

The Pravargya Mantras: Homage to Speech, both that which is uttered and that which is unuttered; homage to that Speech! Homage to Speech! Homage to the Lord of Speech! Homage to the Seers, the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras! May the Seers, the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras, not abandon me; may I not abandon the Seers, the makers of mantras, the lords of mantras. May I utter speech dedicated to all the gods—speech that is auspicious, harmless, and pleasing to the deities. May Heaven grant me shelter; may Earth grant me shelter; may this entire world grant me shelter; may the Moon and the Sun grant me shelter.

Brahmā and Prajāpati! I shall speak of what has been; I shall speak of the world; I shall speak of splendor; I shall speak of glory; I shall speak of austerity; I shall speak of the sacred word (*brahman*); I shall speak of truth. 4. To him I spread this under-layer; may the under-layer be for my offspring and my cattle; may I become an under-layer for my offspring and my cattle. 5. O out-breath and in-breath, protect me from death; O out-breath and in-breath, do not abandon me. 6. I shall think honey; I shall produce honey; I shall speak honey; I shall utter honey. May I raise up speech full of honey for the gods—speech that is worthy of being heard.
May the gods protect him from men; may the ancestors rejoice for the sake of splendor.

They harness the mind and they harness the thoughts—the inspired poets of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, who knows the ways, has established the priestly offices; great is the praise of the god Savitṛ. On the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. Thou art the spade, thou art the woman; thou art the performer of the sacrifice for the gods. Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! We, seeking the gods, entreat thee. May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward.

O Indra, be swift with us. May Brahmanaspati come forward; may the divine Sūnṛtā come forward. May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the manly one who bestows fivefold wealth. O divine Heaven and Earth, may you both favor me. May I succeed today. The head of Makha. For Makha, thee! For the head of Makha, thee! So great wast thou in the beginning. May I succeed today. The head of Makha. For Makha, thee!

For the head of Makha thee! 10. O divine ants, first-born of this being, observers of *ṛta*, may I prosper today! The head of Makha; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee! 11. May I prosper today! The head of Makha; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee! 12. Thou art the vigor of Indra. May I prosper today! The head of Makha; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee! 13. Thou art born of Agni, the seed of Prajāpati. May I prosper today! The head of Makha; for Makha thee; for the head of Makha thee! 14. Bestow life; bestow breath!

Bestow downward breath; bestow pervasive breath. Bestow sight; bestow hearing. Bestow mind; bestow speech. Bestow the self; bestow a firm foundation. Bestow me; bestow [me] upon me. May honey make you honeyed. You are the head of Makha. You two are the feet of the sacrifice. I fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre; I fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre; I fashion you with the Jagatī metre. You are the girdle of Makha. May Aditi grasp your opening.

With the *pāṅkta* metre; with the heat of the sun, be firm. Thou art the sacrifice (*makha*). O Lord, may I prosper today with the head of the sacrifice. The head, the head, thou art the head—nine [syllables]. So great art thou, O Goddess; thou belongest to Indra; thou art born of Agni; bestow long life, bestow breath—five [syllables]. (Anuvāka 3)

You are the drop of the vigorous horse. May Varuṇa, whose vows are firm, fumigate you with the steadfast law of Mitra and Varuṇa. For the flame, you! For the radiance, you! For the light, you! For the heat, you! Mitra, far-extending, has surpassed the heaven in greatness, and the earth in renown. The renown of the god Mitra, the upholder of the people, wins the prize; his splendor possesses most wondrous fame. For success, you! May the divine Savitṛ dig you out.

With beautiful hands, with beautiful fingers, with beautiful arms, and by thy power, standing firm upon the earth, fill the regions and the quarters. Arise and become great; stand upright, for thou art steadfast. With the eye of the Sun I gaze upon thee. For the straight, for the righteous, for a good dwelling, for prosperity—upon thee! Here do I enclose this one, the son of such-and-such a person, with people, with cattle, and with the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*). I cover thee with the *gāyatrī* metre; I cover thee with the *triṣṭubh* metre.
I fortify you with the *jagatī* metre. May speech fortify you; may *ūrk* fortify you; may the oblation fortify you. Fortify speech; fortify strength; fortify the oblation. O God, go forward;
may I accomplish you. Become the earth; do not fail.

O Brahman, we shall proceed with the Pravargya rite. O Hotṛ, praise the Gharma. O Agnīdh, place the two Rauhina cakes on the fire. O Pratiprasthātṛ, distribute the portions. O Prastotṛ, chant the Sāmans. May they bear thee, who art yoked by the Yajus, anointed by the Sāmans, approved by all the gods and the Maruts, extended by the sacrificial gifts, and capable of carrying us across—may they bear thee while thou art well-disposed. Bestowing radiance upon us, do not be angry. Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ. Om! Accompanied by Indra, proceed! Do not be angry. (And the two verses.)

O Brahman, we shall proceed. O Hotṛ, praise the Gharma! For Yama you, for Makha you, for the heat of the Sun you! Svāhā to the out-breath, svāhā to the diffused breath, svāhā to the in-breath! Svāhā to the eye, svāhā to the ear! Svāhā to the mind, svāhā to speech, to Sarasvatī! Svāhā to skill, svāhā to resolve!

Hail to vigor! Hail to strength! 3 May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey. 4 Protect the earth from the heat. 5 You are flame; you are radiance; you are light; you are heat. 6 Sit down together; you are great. Shine forth, O most beloved of the gods! O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, emit your ruddy smoke, O praiseworthy one, visible and beautiful. 7 Him whom the inspired ones anoint as if spreading him out, heating him with fire like a fatty oblation—the most beloved, as a son in the lap of his father.

The cauldron, bringing immortality, has been placed upon Agni. In the invincible east, under the overlordship of Agni, grant me long life. On the south, rich in sons, under the overlordship of Indra, grant me offspring. On the west, providing a good seat, under the overlordship of the god Savitṛ, grant me breath. On the north, the hearer, under the overlordship of Mitra and Varuṇa, grant me hearing. Above, the supporter, under the overlordship of Bṛhaspati, grant me spiritual power (*brahman*), grant me sovereign power (*kṣatra*), and bestow splendor upon me.

Bestow radiance upon me; bestow glory upon me; bestow fervor upon me; bestow mind upon me. 9 You are the mare of the mind, mother of many sons; protect me from all destructive powers. Be easy of access to me; do not harm me. 10 O Agni, burn up the enemies within; burn up those who seek to injure us from afar. Burn up, O Vasu, the thoughtless ones while you are mindful. Let your ageless, tireless flames spread out. 11 You are piled up, you are piled around; with the Maruts, be encompassed by the *svāhā*! 12 You are a stone.

You are the measure; you are the counter-measure; you are the equal-measure; you are the distinct-measure; you are the exceeding-measure; you are the secret hiding-place of the intermediate space. 13. Protect the sky from the heat. 14. O Lord of the Bay Steeds, swelling with these songs, fill up whatever of ours is deficient here. When you shatter the great enclosures for the sake of those who praise you, may we then be the ones who receive the greatest portion of your bounty. 15. One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; like the sky, you possess two days of diverse appearance. For you, O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers.

O Pūṣan, may your auspicious bounty be ours here. You deserve to carry your arrows and your bow; you deserve the worshipful, multiform golden necklace. You deserve to bestow all this world that exists. O Rudra, there is nothing more powerful than you. You are the Gāyatrī; you are the Triṣṭubh; you are the Jagatī. Honey! Honey! Honey! Anoint us! Protect us from the north! You are the image;
yours is another, the worshipful one. You are the Jagatī—this is the nineteenth [verse].

Shine ten times toward the east; shine ten times toward the south; shine ten times toward the west; shine ten times toward the north; shining with a well-disposed mind, shine ten times upward. Bestow radiance upon us, being free from anger. May Agni, together with the Vasus, cause you to shine from the east with the Gāyatrī metre. Once you are made radiant, may he cause me to shine. May Indra, together with the Rudras, cause you to shine from the south with the Triṣṭubh metre. Once you are made radiant, may he cause me to shine. May Varuṇa, together with the Ādityas, cause you to shine from the west with the Jagatī metre.

May he who has shone upon me cause me to shine. May Dyutāna Māruta with the Maruts cause you to shine from the north with the *anuṣṭubh* metre; may he who has shone upon me cause me to shine. May Bṛhaspati with all the gods cause you to shine from above with the *pāṅkta* metre; may he who has shone upon me cause me to shine. (3) O divine Gharma, you have shone among the gods; may I shine among men. (4) O sovereign Gharma, you have shone among the gods; you are long-lived, radiant, and possessed of the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcas*).

May I be pleasing among men; may I, O Long-lived One, be radiant and endowed with the splendor of sacred knowledge (brahmavarcas). 5. You are light. Bestow light upon me. May light be in me. 6. Tenfold you shine in the east; tenfold in the south; tenfold in the west; tenfold in the north; tenfold you shine upward, being well-disposed. As such, O Sovereign, bestow upon us food and vigor. Flow as a prize-winner for the sake of the prize. The heated oblation has been made radiant; may I be radiant. 7. Bestow radiance; bestow it. Nine and [one].

I beheld the herdsman, never resting, moving hither and thither upon his paths; he, clothing himself in converging and diverging rays, revolves repeatedly within the worlds. Here you have helped us, O honeyed ones, with honey and honey-sweetness, for the banquet of the gods. Agni has united with Agni; he shines together with the god Savitṛ, together with Sūrya. Svāhā! Agni has united with fervor; he has united with the god Savitṛ.

He has shone together with the sun; as the sustainer of heaven, you shine through the mid-region; you are the sustainer of the earth, the sustainer of the wide atmosphere, the divine sustainer of the gods, the immortal one born of fervor. I offer you for the heart, I offer you for the mind; I offer you for heaven, I offer you for the sun. Make this sacrifice ascend; bestow the priestly offices among the gods in heaven. O Lord of all beings, Lord of the entire world, Lord of every mind, Lord of every word!

O Lord of all austerity! O Lord of all sacred formulation (*brahman*)! 7 O divine Gharma, you who are heard by the gods, protect the gods! 8 Bestow upon us speech born of austerity that is directed toward the gods. 9 You are the embryo of the gods; 10 the father of thoughts; 11 the lord of progeny; 12 the inspiration of the seers (*kavi*s). 13 The god has united with the god Savitṛ; he has shone together with Sūrya. 14 O Gharma, you are the giver of life to us; you are the giver of splendor. 15 You are our father; as our father, take heed of us! 16 Bestower of life, bestower of bodies, bestower of milk.

Bestower of luster, bestower of space, bestower of wealth; filling the mid-region, more vast than the vast—may we attain thee; do not harm me! (17) O Agni, you are the lord of the household for all human clans. O youngest one, protect me from evil with a hundred fortresses for a hundred winters, protecting the kindler of the flame. May there be wealth, a generous heart, and here indeed let there be gifts! (18) May I consort with you, accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ; possessing good seed, may I deposit my seed. May I obtain a hero in your sight.
May I not be separated from the increase of wealth. 19. For the Sun, I place thee, seeking the gods; may the Giver of Wealth bestow [them]. And two.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. (1) Thou art the girdle of Aditi. (2) O Iḍā, come hither! O Aditi, come hither! O Sarasvatī, come hither! (3) So-and-so, come hither! So-and-so, come hither! So-and-so, come hither! (4) Thou art the turban of Aditi. (5) Vāyu art thou, the Iḍā-calf. (6) May Pūṣan release thee; let the two Aśvins cause thee to flow forth. (7) That breast of thine which is inexhaustible, which is refreshing, wherewith thou nourishest all desirable things—that breast which bestows jewels, finds wealth, and is most bountiful—[that I invoke]. (8)

O Sarasvatī, bring him here for the sake of nourishment; O Dawn, heat the *gharma*—be pleased! O Dawn, protect the *gharma*; be pleased for the sake of the *gharma*. May Bṛhaspati sit down near you. You are the givers, you are the overflowing ones; surrounded on all sides by the red [blood]. Swell for the Aśvins; swell for Sarasvatī; swell for Pūṣan; swell for Bṛhaspati; swell for Indra; swell for Indra. You are of the *gāyatrī* meter; you are of the *triṣṭubh* meter.

Thou art the world; come to me with a portion of vigor. O Indra and Aśvins, drink the honeyed *sāragha* [mead] of the *gharma*; O Vasus, you who are worthy of sacrifice, *vaṭ*! I offer thee, *svāhā*, to the ray of Sūrya, the bringer of rain. Thou art the honeyed oblation; burn with the heat of Sūrya. I encompass thee for Heaven and Earth; I support thee with the intermediate space. Permitted by the gods and the ancestors, may I be able to sustain thee. Thou art brilliance; follow after brilliance.

Do not harm me, thou who touchest heaven! Do not harm me, thou who touchest the intermediate space! Do not harm me, thou who touchest the earth! Thou art the light; grant me the light! Grant me heaven! Protect me from heaven! Come hither! Protect me! Swell! I take [thee]. And nine.

Hail to you, the wind of the ocean! Hail to you, the wind of the waters! Hail to you, the invincible wind! Hail to you, the unassailable wind! Hail to you, the wind that seeks protection! Hail to you, the wind that receives worship! Hail to you, the wind accompanied by *śimidvat*! Hail to you, Agni, accompanied by the Vasus! Hail to you, Soma, accompanied by Rudra! Hail to you, Varuṇa, accompanied by the Ādityas! Hail to you, Bṛhaspati, accompanied by the Viśvedevas!

To Savitṛ, who possesses abundance, who possesses pervasiveness, who possesses sovereignty, and who possesses vigor—svāhā! To Yama, accompanied by the Aṅgirases and the Fathers—svāhā! May he sit as the sacrificial fee for all the quarters; may he sacrifice here to all the gods. Drink of the honeyed Gharma, over which *svāhā* has been uttered, O Aśvins! Svāhā to Agni, worthy of sacrifice! Peace through the *yajus* formulas! O Aśvins, drink the Gharma that gladdens the heart, with your daily protections. May Heaven and Earth grant you their approval.

Svāhā to Indra! 5 Svāhā to Indra! Vaṭ! 6 The Aśvins have drunk the Gharma that gladdens the heart, with their daily aids. May Heaven and Earth grant you approval. That which is to be offered, as prescribed. Homage to Heaven! Homage to Earth! Place this sacrifice in heaven. Place this sacrifice in heaven. Go to heaven. Go to the intermediate space. Go to earth. Go to the five directions. Go to the gods who drink the Gharma. Go to the fathers who drink the Gharma. 7 Svāhā to the possessor of the Ādityas! To the one who gladdens the heart, from the earth—eight [oblations].

Swell for nourishment; swell for strength; swell for the sacred word (*brahman*); swell for the ruling power (*kṣatra*); swell for the waters; swell for the plants; swell for the trees; swell for heaven and earth; swell for well-being; swell for spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*); swell for the sacrificer; swell for me, for my preeminence! For brilliance, thee! For glory, thee! For sensory power, thee! For prosperity, thee! Thou art the Law, the good Law, the one to be honored among us. Uphold the sacred words!

Support the Kṣatriyas; support the Vaiśyas. Let not the wind cause you to fall away. I place you in the breath of so-and-so; go forth to destruction along with him who hates us and whom we hate. To Pūṣan, the sharpener, Svāhā! To the pressing-stones, Svāhā! To the Pratirās, Svāhā! To Heaven and Earth, Svāhā! To the Fathers who drink the Gharma, Svāhā! To Rudra, the Hotṛ, Svāhā! May the Day, with its light as a banner, accept [the offering].

"Good light for the lights, svāhā! May Night, with her banner, enjoy the light. Good light for the lights, svāhā! (7) "Carry me across from day; protect me from night. This is your fuel-stick, O Agni; be kindled by it. Grant me long life; anoint me with splendor. Carry me across from night; protect me from day. This is your fuel-stick, O Agni; be kindled by it. Grant me long life; anoint me with splendor. (8) "Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā!"

The sun is light, light is the sun; *svāhā*! (9) *Bhūḥ* *svāhā*! (10) This is the offered oblation; this is the honeyed oblation. [Offer it] into that fire which belongs to Indra. You are our father; do not harm me. O divine *gharma*, may we partake of you who are honeyed, full of vigor, full of nourishment, belonging to the Aṅgirases, and possessed of the *svadhā* offering. May we enjoy you; do not harm me. (11) *Svāhā* to you for the rays of the sun! *Svāhā* to you for the constellations! (12) Swell for the sake of spiritual luster! Let it flow forth! To Rudra, the Hotṛ, *svāhā*! Protect me from the day in the fire—seven times.

O Gharma, that brilliance of yours which is in heaven, which is in the *gāyatrī* metre, which is in the Brāhmaṇa, which is in the *havirdhāna*—with this I sacrifice it for you; *svāhā*! O Gharma, that brilliance of yours which is in the intermediate space, which is in the *triṣṭubh* metre, which is in the Rājanya, which is in the *āgnīdhra*—with this I sacrifice it for you; *svāhā*! O Gharma, that brilliance of yours which is on earth, which is in the *jagatī* metre, which is in the Vaiśya, which is in the *sadas*—with this I sacrifice it for you; *svāhā*! May Anumati favor us today.

O Anu, O Vidat, O Anumati! For the protection of the highest heaven, I step over you; protect the bodies of the mid-air. By the law of the earth, we step over you for new-found prosperity. For the protection of the highest Brahman, protect the bodies of the Kṣatra. By the law of the Viś, we step over you for new-found prosperity. For the protection of the highest Prāṇa, protect the bodies of the Cakṣus. By the law of the Śrotra...

May we follow after for new prosperity. (6) You are auspicious, O bringer of peace; you are a child, the sustainer of people. (7) Bring us peace and carry us across. (8) The navel of Cosmic Order has four corners. (9) It is the seat, the refuge for all life, the wide-extending shelter. (10) Away with hatred, away with crookedness! We have followed another path of the Vow. (11) O Gharma, this is your food, this is your nourishment. With it, grow and swell; and may we also increase.

And may we be filled [with milk]. 12 You are Ranti, the divine Gandharva; your footprint is the *havirdhāna* (soma-cart); Agni is the overseer; Rudra is the lord. 13 May I be united with long life, united with breath, united with luster, united with milk, united with the state of a herdsman, united with the increase of wealth. 14 Away with that one!—him who hates us and whom we hate. 15 The tawny bull has bellowed; he is great, beautiful to behold like Mitra.

Thou shinest together with the sun; thou art the ocean-born. Indu is skillful, a falcon, the observer of *ṛta*. A golden-winged bird, restless in flight, great and firmly seated in his station. Homage be to thee; do not harm me. The waters, having seen Viśvāvasu, the Gandharva of Soma, went forth according to *ṛta*; they followed after it. Indra, hastening through them, beheld the enclosure of the sun. May Viśvāvasu sing this praise for us.

A divine Gandharva, measuring out the mid-air; whether it be what is true or what we do not know—may he, impelling our thoughts, protect our prayers. 19 He found the winner in the course of the rivers; he threw open the doors of the stone-fenced enclosures. The Gandharva proclaimed their nectarous waters; Indra recognized the skill of the unimpaired one. 20 O divine Gharma, you as a god have approached the gods; here I, a human, [approach] humans. Follow after my drinking of Soma. 21 Here I, a human, [approach] humans. Follow after my drinking of Soma.

Together with progeny, together with the increase of wealth. May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate. We have risen up out of the darkness; [we have seen] that bright one. This most excellent gift for us, this newest song of praise—O Agni, proclaim it among the gods. That which was in the *āgnīdhra* fire-chamber, I have sacrificed for you with this; *svāhā*. Through the Law (*dharman*), may we prosper in the nourishment of *Śaṃyu*. Seated, may we know Tvaṣṭṛ and the *Santv*.

You are the milk of the great [waters], ordained among the gods. You are the light of the trees, the essence of the plants. We, who are strong, lead you, the strong one, downward. May the mind ascend to heaven. Heaven has leaped upon the earth; the young bull has leaped upon the cows. All these worlds have leaped; may the sacrifice, having leaped, procreate. It has leaped, it was born, it has been propagated. From that which has leaped, the bull is born. From that which has leaped, may we propagate ourselves.

The lightning that struck from the east—with this I appease it for you, svāhā! That which [struck] from the south; that which from the west; that which from the north; that lightning which struck from above—with this I appease it for you, svāhā!
To the out-breath, svāhā! To the diffused breath, svāhā! To the in-breath, svāhā! To the eye, svāhā! To the ear, svāhā! To the mind, svāhā! To speech, Sarasvatī, svāhā!

Svāhā to Pūṣan! Svāhā to Pūṣan, the guardian of the ways! Svāhā to Pūṣan, the protector on the path! Svāhā to Pūṣan, who observes men! Svāhā to Pūṣan, the glowing one! Svāhā to Pūṣan, the leader of men! Svāhā to Pūṣan, the one of Sāketa!

Having cast it up with its vital strength, the light bears it, as the earth bears its burden. May the divine *manīṣā* (inspired thought) go forth from us, like a swift chariot fashioned by our skill. Some, chanting, conceived the great *sāman*; by it they sustained the sun; by it they caused the sun to shine. The *gharma* (heated milk) is the head, and that is this fire. You are the soil (*purīṣa*); may you be dear to offspring and cattle. May Prajāpati settle you; through that deity, O Aṅgirasa, sit firm!

O Agni, those wombs of yours which are moist, those which are nest-like; O Agni, those drops of yours and those navels; O Agni, those bodies of yours named "Strength"—with all these, being in harmony with both, sit here, O Agni, with offspring and wealth. May Prajāpati settle you; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

You are Agni; you are Vaiśvānara. You are Saṃvatsara; you are Parivatsara. You are Idāvatsara; you are Iduvatsara. You are Idvatsara; you are Vatsara. Of you, the spring is the head; the summer is the right wing; the rainy season is the tail; the autumn is the left wing; the winter is the center. The bright fortnights are the layers; the dark fortnights are the loose soil. The days and nights are the bricks. May your months and half-months be favorable to you; may the seasons be favorable to you.
May your years be favorable; may your days and nights be favorable. *Ēti*, *prēti*, *vīti*, *sami*, *uditi*. May Prajāpati settle you. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm.

Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Upward indeed for our protection; standing upright, protect us from distress. The grey-haired one has swallowed the young man, who was running about in the assembly of many. Behold the poetic wisdom and majesty of the god: he died today, yet he was the same yesterday. Even without a physical bond, before the devourers could pierce him, Maghavan, the possessor of ancient wealth, joined the joint together.

May you mend what is broken again and again; with vigor and with wealth. O Gharma, do not cause us distress; do not cause us to tremble. Do not cast us down to the lowest place, nor into the dust. Do not place us within the darkness. May the increasing Rudra’s missiles not strike us. O Sunīti, do not abandon us through our failed intentions; do not deliver us to our enemies. May neither Rudra nor Nirṛti, nor the archer, nor Heaven and Earth be angry with us. O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect us here!

May you two, O friends, kindle [the fire] for us here. The snare of the Ādityas is a weapon; may that fierce one with a hundred points spare us on every side. 7. This [is my prayer]; O Varuṇa, I entreat you according to truth. You, O Agni, are ours; as such, you, O Agni, are ours. You, O Agni, are the messenger. 8. We have risen up out of the darkness. Up that [sun], the bright, the birds with beautiful wings. 9. May the two Suparṇas, possessing wealth before them, be gracious.

Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! In me be that great power of Indra; in me be skill, in me be wisdom; in me has been placed heroic vigor. May the three-fold Gharma shine for me, together with intention and mind, with sovereign splendor and light, with sacrifice and milk, with sacred formulation and brilliance, with dominion and glory, with truth and austerity. May we partake of its milking; may we partake of its favor; may we partake of its enjoyment.
Of this, which has been drunk by Indra, which is honey-sweet, which has been invited—I, being invited, partake.

Those terrible forms of yours, O Agni—hunger and thirst; exhaustion and lack of oblation; famishing and parching; exhaustion and delusion—these are your terrible forms, O Agni. With these, go to him who hates us and whom we hate.
Clinging, oozing, and melting; heat and cold; fierce and terrifying; ever-consumptive and wasting—these are your terrible forms, O Agni. With these, go to him who hates us and whom we hate.
Shaker and darkness and roar and roaring and thundering; besmearing and smearing and scattering—1.
Fierce and shaker and darkness and roar and roaring and thundering; the victorious and the conquering and the victor and the more victorious; having come and having gone away, the scatterers—1.
May day and night impel you! May the half-months drive you forth! May the months cook you! May the seasons ripen you! May the year slay you, O so-and-so! 1.

*Khaphaṭ jahī! Chindhi bhindhi handhi kaṭ!* These are cruel words. O Indra, as they wander about, cause them to be caught; O Indra, while they sleep, seek out their cattle. With the thunderbolt, awaken that one who is difficult to find. Strike him while he sleeps, away from his provisions. O Agni, converse with Agni; O Death, converse with Death. Homage be to you, O Blessed One. Once, O Agni, homage to you; twice, homage to you; thrice, homage to you; four times, homage to you; five times, homage to you; ten times, homage to you; a hundred times, homage to you.

Homage to you a thousand times! Homage to you immeasurable times! Let there be homage to you; do not harm me! 3 With mouth of raw flesh, indistinct with blood, you run about as Yama’s messenger, O dog-footed one. You, a vulture, a great-winged bird, haunt the corpse. You are dispatched as the messenger of both Yama and Bhava. 1
When you, having become a wolf, O Goddess Speech, howl—howl at my enemy! O Death, lead him away to death; let him meet with affliction through affliction.
Whether incited by others or acting of his own will, when the jackal utters this speech, may Indra and Agni, in harmony with the sacred word (*brahman*), make it auspicious for us within our homes.
O long-faced one of ill-jaw, do not howl from the south! If you should howl from the south, drive away my enemy.
Thus has the owl swooped down, golden-eyed and iron-beaked; the messenger of the *rakṣases* has arrived. O Agni, destroy him from here!

When you have entered into these beings and speak the divine speech, proclaim our enemies far away. O Death, lead them unto death; let them meet with calamity through their own affliction. Let fire converse with fire;
you fly about with legs outstretched, and you blink your left eye. May no one here suffer harm.

I kill you, O worm, with Atri; with Kaṇva, with Jamadagni. Slain by the sacred spell of Viśvāvasu is the king of worms; even their chieftain is slain. And so the mother, and so the father; and so the large ones, and so the small ones! And so the black ones, and so the white ones; and so the *āśātikās* are slain. All are slain along with the white ones. Bring [the portion] today, as of the cooked oblation—that is the truth. That which I place within the jaws of Yama for him, so indeed shall it be. *Khaṇphaṇmrasi*.

I curse you with the *brahman*. I curse you with the oath of the *brahman*. I gaze upon you with the terrible eye of the Bhṛgus. I meditate upon you with the fierce mind of the Aṅgirases. I pierce you with the stream of evil. Fall down lower than me, O so-and-so! Strike him, O destroyer of the *śimi*! Strike him down on his bed, O one born on the bed! Make him enter the mountains! Drive him into the rays of light! As far as the sun rises from here in the east, so far from here destroy that person who hates us and whom we hate!

Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Bhuvo 'ddhāyi, bhuvo 'ddhāyi, bhuvo 'ddhāyi! Nṛmṇāyi nṛmṇam, nṛmṇāyi nṛmṇam, nṛmṇāyi nṛmṇam! Nidhāyyo 'vāyi, nidhāyyo 'vāyi, nidhāyyo 'vāyi! E asme asme! Suvar na jyotiḥ!

The earth is the fuel. Agni kindles it; it kindles Agni; I kindle it. May it, being kindled, kindle me with long life, with splendor, with radiance, with prosperity, with fame, with the luster of sacred knowledge, and with the food of nourishment—svāhā! The atmosphere is the fuel. Vāyu kindles it; it kindles Vāyu; I kindle it. May it, being kindled, kindle me with long life, with splendor, with radiance, with prosperity, with fame, with the luster of sacred knowledge, and with the food of nourishment—svāhā! The sky is the fuel. Āditya kindles it...

He kindles her together with the sun; may I kindle her. May she, being kindled, kindle me with long life, with splendor, with luster, with prosperity, with fame, with the luster of sacred knowledge, and with the food of nourishment—*svāhā*! 3. You are the fuel of Prajāpati for me, the destroyer of rivals; you are the slayer of my enemies, *svāhā*! 4. O Agni, lord of vows, I shall perform the vow.

May I be able to do that; may it be successful for me. O Vāyu, Lord of Vows! O Āditya, Lord of Vows! O Lord of Vows, Lord of vows, I shall perform the vow. May I be able to do that; may it be successful for me. 5. Heaven is the fuel. Āditya kindles it; he kindles Āditya; I kindle him. Kindled by me, may it [endow] me with long life and splendor.

May she kindle me with splendor, with glory, with fame, with the luster of sacred knowledge, with food, Svāhā! The atmosphere is the fuel; Vāyu kindles it, and it kindles Vāyu. I kindle it; may it, being kindled, kindle me with long life, with brilliance, with splendor, with glory, with fame, with the luster of sacred knowledge, and with food, Svāhā! The earth is the fuel; Agni kindles it, and it kindles Agni. I kindle it; may it, being kindled, kindle me with long life, with brilliance, with splendor, with glory, with fame, and with the luster of sacred knowledge.

May they kindle me with food; *svāhā*! You are my fuel, belonging to Prajāpati, the destroyer of rivals. You are the slayer of my enemies; *svāhā*! O Āditya, Lord of Vows, I have performed the vow. I was able to do it; it has been successful for me. O Vāyu, Lord of Vows! O Agni, Lord of Vows! O Lord of Vows among vows, I have performed the vow. I was able to do it; it has been successful for me. (6) The fuel kindles the fuel. I shall perform the vow with splendor, prosperity, fame, and the luster of sacred knowledge—eight and [the rest].

May Vāta, Mātariśvan, blow auspiciously for us; may Sūrya shine auspiciously for us. May the days be auspicious for us; may the night be established as auspicious. May Uṣas dawn upon us with peace; may Āditya rise for our well-being. O Sarasvatī, be gracious, most auspicious, and most merciful to us.

May it not be visible to you from the sky. You are the dwelling-place of *iḍā*; may we be possessed of a dwelling-place; may we never be deprived of our dwelling-place. May he who hates us and whom we hate be without a dwelling-place. (3) You are the firm foundation; may we be possessed of a firm foundation; may we never be deprived of our foundation. May he who hates us and whom we hate be without a foundation. (4) O Wind, blow hither healing; O Wind, blow away whatever is harmful. For you, as the messenger of the gods, go forth as the possessor of all healing remedies. (5) These two winds blow: one from the ocean and one from the far distance.

May one wind blow skillfully for me; may the other blow away whatever is harmful. 6. O Vāta, that treasure of immortality which is placed in your house yonder—grant us from it so that we may live; grant us from it healing medicine; bring us from it great prosperity. 7. May Vāta blow healing medicine toward us—beneficent and bringing delight to our heart; may he prolong our lives. 8. You are the house of Indra; I enter you, along with my cattle and my horses.

Whatever I possess, with that—9. I take refuge in *bhūḥ*; I take refuge in *bhuvaḥ*; I take refuge in *suvaḥ*; I take refuge in *bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ*; I take refuge in Vāyu; I take refuge in the unafflicted deity; I take refuge in the unbroken stone; I take refuge in the Brahman-treasury of Prajāpati; I take refuge in Brahman; I take refuge in *oṃ*. 10. May the wide, great intermediate space be my refuge; may the fires and the mountains, and that well-being by which the wind blows—by that well-being, may my vital breaths be safe. 11. O Prāṇa and Apāna, protect me from death!

May out-breath and in-breath not forsake me. May Agni bestow wisdom upon me, offspring upon me, and splendor upon me; may Indra bestow wisdom upon me, offspring upon me, and sensory power upon me; may Sūrya bestow brilliance upon me.

O Aśvins, protect us with unharmed blessings day and night. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us. (14) With what aid will the wonderful one come to us, he who is the friend ever-increasing? With what most powerful company? (15) Which true exhilaration of the juices shall intoxicate you most, so that you may break open even the firmest wealth? (16) Come to us as the protector of our friends and singers.

May you be with us with a hundred aids. 17 The Priyamedha seers, like strong-winged birds, have approached Indra with their supplications: Dispel the darkness, fill our eyes with light, and release us as if we were bound in a snare! 18

May the divine Waters be auspicious for our aid and for our drinking; may they flow toward us with peace and well-being. (19) I beg the Waters—the sovereign lords of desirable things, who dwell among the people—for their healing medicine. (20) May the Waters and the Plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate. (21) O Waters, you are indeed the sources of bliss; grant us strength, so that we may behold great joy. (22) Grant us a share here of that most auspicious sap which belongs to you.

Like longing mothers, [come] to him for whose abode you quicken; O Waters, give us life. 24 The earth is peaceful; it is pacified by Agni. May it, being pacified, appease my heat. 25 The atmosphere is peaceful; it is pacified by Vāyu. May it, being pacified, appease my heat. 26 The sky is peaceful; it is pacified by Āditya. May it, being pacified, appease my heat. 27 The earth is peace, the atmosphere is peace, the sky is peace, the quarters are peace, the intermediate quarters are peace, Agni is peace, Vāyu is peace, Āditya is peace, and the Moon is peace.

Peace are the stars; peace are the waters; peace are the herbs; peace are the trees; peace is the cow; peace is the goat; peace is the horse; peace is man; peace is the *brahman*; peace is the *brāhmaṇa*; peace indeed is peace; may peace be mine—peace! (28) By that peace, by all-encompassing peace, I bring peace for my two-footed and four-footed beings; may peace be mine—peace! (29) Hither come Prosperity, Modesty, Fortitude, Austerity, Intelligence, Stability, Faith, and Truth.

May Dharma follow me as I rise; may Fortune, Modesty, Fortitude, Austerity, Intelligence, Stability, Faith, Truth, and Dharma not abandon me. (30) With long life, with good life, with the essence of plants, and with the vigor of Parjanya, I have risen up after the immortals. (31) That eye, beneficial to the gods, the bright one, has risen in the east.

May we see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns; may we rejoice for a hundred autumns; may we delight for a hundred autumns; may we be present for a hundred autumns; may we hear for a hundred autumns; may we speak forth for a hundred autumns; may we remain unconquered for a hundred autumns, and may we long behold the sun. He who has risen from the great ocean, shining forth from the midst of the flood—may that bull, the red-eyed Sun, the wise one, purify me with his mind. You are the dripping of the *brahman*, you are the axle-pin of the *brahman*.

You are the vessel for the sacred word (*brahman*). By the sacred word this great earth is supported; by it the great intermediate space is supported; it has upheld the sky and the earth together with the gods. What I know, that may I maintain; let not my knowledge fall away from me. (34) May wisdom and insight enter me, united, for the attainment of what has been and what is to be.
